clue.text: Stone, a short time before last of Viagra, gains endurance

parts.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for stone, the weight
taken as written
a minute, shortened to its abbreviation

indicators.note: last of asks only for the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of the drug's name

explanation.surface: A man takes a pill shortly before the big moment and finds he can last longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places the minute ahead of the last letter of Viagra.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the staying power to keep going, which is what endurance means.

clue.text: Brenda gets a rise, lots of money, possibly worth another extension?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, ER

indicators.note: possibly suggests the word could be rearranged into some other form

parts.note: G is a grand, a thousand pounds
the word to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Queen gets a pay rise worth a fortune, and perhaps it is worth extending her reign.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running name for Queen Elizabeth II, so she supplies the royal cipher ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or tissue that grows back is regrowth, a further lengthening after the first, hence an extension again.

clue.text: "Used GM produces" smear

indicators.note: produces suggests the quoted words are worked up into something new

parts.note: the quoted letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A green campaigner's slogan against genetically modified crops, quoted as if it were a smear campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a dirty blurred mark, the same thing as a smear.

clue.text: A frequent activity of politicians: one gin and erectile dysfunction

indicators.note: a dysfunction is a failure to work properly, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the first part of the material to be rearranged
the rest of the material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dig that a politician's typical problem is a drink too many and a failure to perform in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Electioneering is campaigning for votes, something politicians do constantly.

clue.text: Spears possibly giving Cyclops wind up arse

parts.note: the setter, Cyclops, refers to himself
wind in the bowels is gas

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the following word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: loosely, rat as in rat-arsed; written upwards

explanation.surface: A crude image of the setter getting a blast of wind from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The link from arse to the final three letters is loose: the setter seems to lean on rat-arsed, or on Rats! and Arse! as interchangeable curses. Spears is Britney Spears, the pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Britney Spears is an example of a huge celebrity, a megastar, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Gordon "cherishes" hospital section? Makes you spit!

definitions.note: a verb phrase for a noun: what makes you spit

indicators.note: to cherish is to hold close, so one part is held inside the other

parts.note: Gordon Brown was Prime Minister
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
a leg is one section of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's fondness for the health service is enough to make anyone spit.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon means Gordon Brown, then Prime Minister, so the outer letters are his title PM.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm is thick mucus from the throat, the stuff that a person coughs up and spits out.

clue.text: Corsets put in place, as Brenda does to annoy her waiting son?

definitions.text: as Brenda does to annoy her waiting son?

parts.note: stays are an old word for a corset
clothes put in place are on

explanation.surface: The Queen keeps her corset firmly on and keeps her heir waiting for the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, and her waiting son is Prince Charles, kept from the throne for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain in post, which the Queen did, leaving her heir still waiting.

clue.text: Jollies associated with Gore's hot air

parts.note: Jollies is a nickname for the Royal Marines, giving THE RM
Al Gore, the US vice-president and climate campaigner

explanation.surface: A sneer that Al Gore's climate talk is so much hot air, linked to his fun trips.
explanation.walkthrough: Jollies is old service slang for the Royal Marines, so it stands for THE RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising current of warm air, used by gliders and birds.

clue.text: Take off before this cracks nuts!

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic or ape them

indicators.note: something that cracks breaks up, so its letters come apart and reassemble

parts.note: the word to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nutcracker's advice: take the shell off before this tool breaks the nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Going apeshit is crude slang for going crazy, so it means mad or nuts.

clue.text: 'Hot bot' I stimulated with feather — rather coy sex

indicators.note: stimulated letters are stirred up and moved about into a new order

parts.note: the first part of the letters to be rearranged
the rest of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A saucy scene of a bottom tickled with a feather, offered as tame lovemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit of the other is a coy British euphemism for having sex.

clue.text: Skirt put back on Rebekah Wade in the bog?

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the other way, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: to skirt is to edge, and an edge is a rim
Rebekah Wade was editor of the Sun, an ED

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor caught pulling her skirt back on in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like the garment but is the verb meaning to go round the edge. Rebekah Wade, later Brooks, edited the Sun and News of the World.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog here is a marsh rather than a toilet, and to be mired is to be stuck in mud.

clue.text: Political deception turns of course on Tory nos. 1 and 2 going

the party member, before trimming

explanation.surface: Tory leaders quitting is set among the twists and turns of political trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but is literal: the course is a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery and underhand dodging, the deceit politicians are accused of.

clue.text: State of ex-con: "I'm pissed, being shafted by flipping Private Eye!"

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over so it reads the other way
to be shafted is to be penetrated, so another piece is pushed inside
pissed is crude slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the magazine speaks of itself as we, written backwards

explanation.surface: A drunken former convict complains about being stitched up by the magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of ex-con' suggests a condition; the state is a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexico is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Casual love making speed

parts.note: a temp is a casual worker
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Casual sex rushed through at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love making' reads as lovemaking, but 'making' is just the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the rate or pace at which music or activity moves, so it means speed.

clue.text: A certain tone set by a couple of tits and a freak PM

parts.note: a pair of breasts sits on the chest
a freak or fanatic is a nut
Gordon Brown, the Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A political jibe that the tone is set by a pair of idiots and an odd Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tits' here also reads as fools, but the wordplay wants breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut brown is a particular reddish-brown colour, a shade or tone.

clue.text: Dashing fellow, John Thomas out to shock the public

definitions.text: Dashing fellow, John Thomas out to shock the public

parts.note: surface reading: a stylish, debonair man about to cause a scandal

parts.words: John Thomas out to shock the public
parts.note: setter's reading: a man running naked with his penis on show, John Thomas being slang for it

explanation.walkthrough: Dashing means literally running, and John Thomas is British slang for the penis, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs naked through a public place, often a sports ground, to shock or amuse.

clue.text: Sort of lies often put out on Page 3?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: very large breasts, as shown by the topless models of the Sun's Page 3

explanation.walkthrough: Page 3 of the Sun newspaper long carried a photo of a topless model; whoppers is slang for anything very big.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is anything enormous, so a big fib or, crudely, a big breast.

clue.text: Rich is one UK political leader capturing Bush's heart

parts.note: one is the article a

indicators.note: capturing means taking hold of, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: Ming Campbell led the Liberal Democrats

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of the president's name

explanation.surface: A wry line that a British party leader is wealthy now he has the US president on side.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Menzies 'Ming' Campbell led Britain's Liberal Democrats in 2006-07.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich in the sense of 'that's rich' means highly entertaining or laughable.

clue.text: Ill-tempered as Sweeney Todd could get

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sulky and bad-tempered, prone to strops
second meaning, a joke: the murderous barber sharpening his razor on a leather strop

explanation.walkthrough: A strop is both a tantrum and the leather strap barbers use to hone a razor; Sweeney Todd is the fictional demon barber.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for bad-tempered and difficult, someone having a strop.

clue.text: Ex-PM's holiday destination — initially Cherie arranged to go

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's holiday plans, with Cherie Blair having arranged to come along.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major was British Prime Minister before Tony Blair, so he is a former PM.

clue.text: Waggish Stalin's holding companies?

parts.note: Joseph Stalin was known as Uncle Joe
COS is the plural abbreviation for companies

explanation.surface: A joke that Stalin, of all people, liked to keep a grip on businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and joking, just as waggish describes a wit or joker.

clue.text: "Organ's bust!", screamed out by sergeant-major?

parts.note: the eye is an organ, with the possessive S
a woman's bust is her front

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks that an organ is broken, as a drill sergeant might bellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as broken but is the chest; 'Organ' suggests a musical instrument but is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes front is a parade-ground command to look straight ahead, barked by a drill sergeant.

clue.text: One who tosses female off, geddit? (Not Dee)

clue.text: Brown is supposed to be so convivial — it's hopeless!

clue.text: Pickpockets love an alkie

love is zero in tennis, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Thieves who are fond of a drunk, an easy mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipso, short for dipsomaniac, is slang for an alcoholic, as is alkie.

clue.text: Funds, say, put into filthy Gents

explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is a store of savings set aside for later, a sum of money.

clue.text: Magazine decline that makes you blink?

definitions.note: a verb phrase for a noun: something that makes you blink

parts.note: Private Eye, the magazine itself
a decline is a drop

explanation.surface: A fall in the magazine's sales is enough to make you blink.
